This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Amsterdam Airport Schiphol Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eham

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **The market's overwhelming 99.9% implied probability on a 20°C high reflects the tight clustering of official forecasts around that exact threshold.** Multiple numerical weather prediction runs, including GFS guidance, project a daytime maximum near 20°C (68–69°F) for Amsterdam on September 5 under partly cloudy skies, moderate westerly flow around 15–20 mph, and negligible precipitation. This aligns closely with the 1991–2020 climatological average high of roughly 20.3°C for the date. Late-day observations from nearby stations such as Schiphol are expected to confirm the peak before cooling into the mid-teens overnight. Only a substantial, unanticipated model error or highly localized microclimate spike could push readings outside the narrow 20°C bin, an outcome traders currently assign negligible odds given the stable synoptic pattern.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Dallas Love Field Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kdal

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Current meteorological guidance for Panama City, Panama, points to a daytime maximum near 30 °C amid typical September convective activity, with afternoon thunderstorms and high humidity (around 75–90 %) expected to limit peak readings.** Recent model consensus from regional forecasts shows scattered showers developing by midday, which historically caps temperatures through cloud shading and evaporative cooling, keeping values close to the long-term September average high of 30 °C. The tight market split between 33 °C and 34 °C-plus outcomes reflects uncertainty in the precise timing and coverage of convection: delayed or lighter rainfall could permit a brief late-morning or early-afternoon spike above 32 °C, while earlier or heavier storms would suppress it. Official observations and updated short-range guidance expected later today will clarify whether conditions favor the lower or upper side of that narrow band.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent cloud cover and widespread rainfall are capping daytime heating in Tokyo on September 6, keeping the highest temperature centered on 23–24°C according to official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble models.** Northerly to northeasterly flow advects cooler, moist air while thick stratiform clouds sharply reduce incoming solar radiation, limiting surface warming despite late-summer insolation potential. Updated JMA and global model runs through the evening of September 5 will provide the final resolution inputs.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent southwest monsoon (Habagat) activity is the primary driver keeping Manila’s maximum temperature on September 6 centered near 29–30 °C.** Official PAGASA outlooks and multiple model runs indicate cloudy skies, scattered to occasional showers and thunderstorms, and moderate-to-strong southwesterly winds, all of which reduce solar insolation and cap daytime heating. Recent days have followed the same pattern, with observed highs in the upper 20s to low 30s under similar monsoon flow.  

September climatology shows average highs near 31 °C, but the active monsoon phase typically suppresses peaks by several degrees through persistent cloud cover and evaporative cooling from rain. Current forecasts from global and regional models cluster tightly around 28–30 °C, producing the market’s strong weighting toward 30 °C (44.5 %) and 29 °C (28.5 %). Final resolution depends on the official PAGASA or Ninoy Aquino International Airport maximum reading; any unexpected clearing could push readings toward 31 °C, while heavier or more prolonged rain would favor 28 °C or below.

Traders are weighting the 27°C and 28°C outcomes most heavily because subtle differences in rain timing, wind speed, and localized clearing could shift the recorded high by 1–2°C. With resolution depending on the precise maximum at the Tokyo official station, the tight spread among leading probabilities mirrors genuine forecast uncertainty in the final 48 hours before the market settles.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Helsinki Vantaa Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=efhk

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Recent National Weather Service and model guidance for Houston on September 7 points to mostly sunny conditions with a modest chance of afternoon thunderstorms, supporting highs in the low to mid-90s.** This aligns with early September climatology, where the 1991–2020 average high is 90.8 °F, though recent days have featured readings in the mid-90s amid humid, unstable air. Light steering winds and limited upper-level support for strong cooling keep temperatures from surging into the upper 90s or dropping below the low 90s. Trader emphasis on the 92–95 °F range reflects this consensus, tempered by typical model variability in convective timing and any last-minute forecast adjustments from the National Hurricane Center or local offices before the Labor Day period.

Historical September climatology shows average highs near 30°C, with recent observations and short-range guidance (including GFS and local IMHPA inputs) aligning closely without major deviations such as suppressed convection or anomalous ridging. Trader consensus favoring 31°C (40.5% implied probability) and 32°C (27%) reflects this central tendency, while the modest 13.5% on 33°C+ accounts for upside potential if storms develop later or steering patterns allow greater insolation.
